items.title: Y.S.P. Industries taps value-conscious consumers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Y.S.P. Industries (M) Sdn Bhd (YSPI) is expanding its wellness brand into skincare, tapping into a consumer market where affordability, value and everyday self-care are increasingly shaping purchasing decisions. The move also reflects a broader convergence within the consumer industry, with health, wellness, beauty and personal care increasingly overlapping as consumers seek products that support both physical wellbeing and confidence.

items.title: Bukit Aman denies police MPV escorted cable theft vehicle in Ampang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Police have denied claims circulating online that a Mobile Patrol Vehicle (MPV) escorted a vehicle believed to be carrying stolen cables in Kampung Tasik Tambahan, Ampang, last Saturday. Sinar Harian reported that Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation and Community Safety Department director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said police had arrested a cable theft suspect in connection with the incident. He said claims that the police vehicle was involved in a conspiracy with the cable thieves were untrue.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher against US Dollar, major currencies on improved sentiment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened slightly higher against the US dollar and a basket of major currencies on Tuesday, supported by improved market sentiment amid easing global oil prices and geopolitical developments. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude oil prices fell 3.4 per cent to US$100.34 per barrel, following satellite data showing that Saudi Arabia had shifted its oil exports via the Strait of Hormuz after the East-West pipeline shut down. It was reported that Saudi Arabia has increased its crude oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz to about 2.9 million barrels per day, from around 700,000 barrels per day in August, following the disruption to the East-West pipeline.

items.title: China and Europe should not fight trade wars
items.summary: BEIJING: China and Europe should not fight trade wars because the pair are comprehensive strategic partners, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi told his German counterpart in a call, according to a statement from Beijing. "China and the EU are comprehensive strategic partners; China and Europe should not fight trade wars," a statement from the ministry cited Wang as saying. Germany's foreign ministry said the two ministers agreed that a stable global economy is in China's, Germany's and Europe's interest.

items.title: Green policies just good politics, says UK minister
items.summary: United Nations, United States: Transitioning to a low-carbon economy isn't just vital for the planet's future – it's also good politics, according to Britain's climate minister, who argues the country's record-hot summer has galvanised public opinion like never before. Katie White, a member of the ruling Labour government, said the UK's right-wing parties had miscalculated by vowing to undo the country's greenhouse gas goals if they took power. "The UK public is hugely in favour of action on climate," said the minister of state in the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero during an interview with AFP at the United Nations headquarters in New York on Monday.

items.title: Malaysia backs Saudi sovereignty, calls for end to Houthi hostilities
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia has condemned in the strongest terms the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and expressed solidarity with the Kingdom. Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry said Malaysia supported Saudi Arabia’s efforts to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the security and safety of its population, in accordance with the United Nations Charter and international law. The Foreign Ministry said Malaysia reaffirmed the importance of its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties.

items.title: Man shot by ICE describes pain of bullet still inside him
items.summary: AUSTIN, (Texas): A Venezuelan national shot and wounded by a US immigration agent in Texas was jailed with the bullet still inside his body, his lawyer said Monday. Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, 28, told reporters he was delivering an order for DoorDash on Sunday when his vehicle was rammed by an ICE agent and he was shot. Garces Perez said.

items.title: EUDR rules bring clarity for Malaysian planters, limited impact seen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The finalisation of the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) regulatory framework is expected to provide greater implementation clarity for Malaysian planters ahead of the regulation's application from end-Dec 2026. Compared to the delegated act, Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) said the implementing act has a much smaller impact on oil palm plantation companies. Overall, HLIB believes Malaysian planters, particularly those with established exposure to the EU market, are well positioned for the EUDR's implementation.

items.title: Education Ministry opens private schools sector to all investors, no more 30pc Bumi rule
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 22 — A minimum of 30 per cent Bumiputera equity ownership is no longer a requirement for private limited companies operating private educational institutions (IPS) under the Ministry of Education (MOE). The ministry said the decision was reached following discussions with the Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry. The ministry noted the concerns raised regarding the 30 per cent Bumiputera equity requirement for specific IPS owned by private limited companies, as outlined in the IPS Policy Statement Book published in 2006.

items.title: Orang Asli man killed in suspected tiger attack while searching for rotan in Sungai Siput
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — An Orang Asli man was killed after he was believed to have been attacked by a tiger while searching for rotan in a forest area near Kampung Takung, Pos Perwor in Sungai Siput yesterday. Sinar Harian reported that Zamberi Angah, 42, was found dead in a bamboo clump near a logging road, about 200 metres from where the attack was believed to have taken place. The Malay daily reported that Zamberi was found at about 6.58pm in a bamboo clump near the logging road.

items.title: Gamuda orderbook seen hitting RM60bil as contract pipeline builds
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd's orderbook could rise to RM60 billion by year-end, about 20 per cent above its target, as strong contract wins and a visible pipeline support earnings growth, according to CGS International Securities Malaysia Sdn Bhd. Gamuda's latest A$624 million (about RM1.8 billion) Australian contract takes its FY27 year-to-date order wins to RM10.2 billion, lifting its orderbook to RM62.5 billion as at September 2026, CGS said. CGS estimates Gamuda will end CY26 with an orderbook of RM55 billion to RM56 billion, about 10 per cent above its RM50 billion target, assuming a monthly orderbook burn rate of RM1 billion and no further contract wins.

items.title: Illegal activities in prisons: A question of control, not perfection
items.summary: From a criminological perspective, however, it is important to distinguish between allegations or individual incidents and evidence of the overall prevalence of illegal activity across the prison system. The reality is that illegal activities occur in prison systems around the world. Singer-composer Muhammad Yasin Sulaiman alleged that drugs could still enter prison despite stringent security procedures.

items.title: Maritime industry expert seeks Customs dept ruling on RM220m K8 cargoes, calls for industry-wide SOP on petroleum blending
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) has been urged to issue a clear written position on the Customs treatment of two petroleum cargoes with a combined declared value exceeding RM220 million, as continued uncertainty could affect shipping agents, terminal operators, cargo owners and other participants in Malaysia’s downstream petroleum sector. Maritime Network Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan said the company was not asking JKDM to decide the matter in its favour, but to state the applicable law, procedure and documentary requirements in writing. The matter concerns two Atlanta Crude Oil cargoes totalling 76,954.325 metric tonnes.

items.title: Malaysia taps Gulf air links to grow Middle East tourism
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Malaysia is strengthening air connectivity and tourism cooperation with the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and the wider Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) region to boost tourist arrivals from the Middle East. According to Tourism Malaysia’s statement today, among the key outcomes were the signing of Memorandums of Understanding between Tourism Malaysia with Emirates and Qatar Airways to strengthen tourism promotion and joint marketing efforts. Also present was Tourism Malaysia director-general Mohd Amirul Rizal Abdul Rahim.

items.title: Fire damages classroom at Chung Ling in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A classroom at Sekolah Menengah Jenis Kebangsaan Chung Ling in Air Itam was damaged in a fire last night. Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the department received a distress call at 7.54pm. Firefighters from the Paya Terubong and Lebuh Pantai fire and rescue stations brought the blaze under control at 8.16pm and extinguished it within 25 minutes.

items.title: Newly opened Pinglu Canal to enhance Malaysia-China, Asean trade connectivity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The opening of China's Pinglu Canal on Sept 16 could further enhance trade connectivity between Malaysia, China and the wider Asean region. CGTN reporter Xu Hua shared this during the Bernama World programme on Monday, speaking virtually on "China-Asean Expo (CAEXPO) 2026: Malaysia, China & The Future of Asean Trade". On the China-Asean Free Trade Area (CAFTA) 3.0 upgrade, Xu Hua said the agreement represented a fundamental shift in economic cooperation, moving beyond conventional trade in goods toward digital economy development, green industries, and stronger regional supply chains.

items.title: Flights scrapped, evacuations urged as Typhoon Dujuan wallops Japan
items.summary: TOKYO: More than one million people were under evacuation advisories in Japan early Tuesday and hundreds of flights have been cancelled as Typhoon Dujuan brushed past Tokyo, bringing torrential rains, flooding and landslides to the region. Two people have been confirmed dead as heavy rainfall triggered landslides in Chiba and Kanagawa prefectures near Tokyo, local governments reported, according to Japanese media including the Kyodo news agency. Dujuan was bringing winds of some 144km per hour Monday as it moved to around 130 kilometres south of Katsuura City near Tokyo.

items.title: Saudi strike kills 6 in Yemen port city Mokha: Houthi media
items.summary: SANAA, (Yemen): Saudi strikes on the strategic Red Sea port city of Mokha killed at least six people and wounded eight others, the group's affiliated news agency Saba reported Tuesday. "Six civilians, including two children and a woman, were killed and eight others, including a child and a woman, were injured in Saudi-led coalition airstrikes on Mokha," it said. The Houthis, who control large parts of northwest Yemen, seized Mokha earlier this month after launching a large-scale attack against Yemeni government forces, who are backed by Saudi Arabia.

items.title: US to open two new military bases in Greenland
items.summary: COPENHAGEN/WASHINGTON: The US plans to reopen a former Cold War-era military base in southern Greenland and set up a military presence at an east coast base now used by the Danish dog sled patrol under an agreement to be signed by the US, Denmark and Greenland on Tuesday, according to three people familiar with the matter. Denmark, Greenland and the US are expected to sign their new agreement at the United Nations General Assembly in New York City at 10.30am ET (1430 GMT) on Tuesday. Today only Pituffik Space Base remains, with some 150 US military personnel.

items.title: UK agrees support for Saudi in struggle with Houthis
items.summary: LONDON: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has agreed to give military support to Saudi Arabia to help it tackle attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis, media reports said on Monday. British planes will provide "defensive" air-to-air refuelling for Saudi jets, he told reporters as he travelled to the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The refuelling mission is in addition to the UK Sky Sabre air defence system already deployed in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Malaysia's EV policy becomes more decisive, puts local value first: MAA president
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's electric vehicle (EV) policy has become more decisive with the government seeking to ensure the shift towards electric mobility translates into local assembly, technology transfer and a stronger domestic supply chain. MAA president Mohd Shamsor Mohd Zain said Malaysia's approach differs from Thailand's move to raise excise taxes on imported EVs. "For fully imported EVs, Malaysia now applies a 30 per cent import duty, 10 per cent excise duty and 10 per cent sales tax.

items.title: Bernama, TASS sign MoU to strengthen news cooperation
items.summary: MOSCOW: The Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama) and Russian News Agency TASS on Monday signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to strengthen cooperation in news and multimedia content exchange, professional expertise, and emerging technologies. The MOU was signed by Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin and TASS Director-General Andrey Kondrashov in conjunction with the 65th anniversary of the Organisation of Asia-Pacific News Agencies (OANA) here. "Today, news travels across borders within seconds.

items.title: Lebanon needs international force after peacekeepers leave, PM tells UN chief
items.summary: BEIRUT: Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam told United Nations chief Antonio Guterres on Monday that Lebanon needed a UN-sponsored international force to stay in the country's south after the current UN peacekeeping mandate expires. The UN Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL), which currently counts around 7,500 peacekeepers from 46 countries, has acted as a buffer between Lebanon and Israel since 1978. UNIFIL's looming departure comes as Israel maintains troops in a self-declared "security zone" running around 10km (six miles) deep inside south Lebanon along the border.

items.title: ''We cannot defy their orders': Warden alleges senior officers facilitate smuggling'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: "Rizal", a Kajang Prison warden in his 30s who has served in the prison service for less than 10 years, said he had seen how inmates tested the limits of prison security. He said prison officers were required to search inmates returning from court, hospital visits and other authorised movements outside their blocks. Rizal said officers also had to watch for inmates using work assignments or movements within the prison to pass prohibited items between blocks.

items.title: From Op Piramid to MH370: Five decades of RMAF Hercules service
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: For five decades, the Lockheed C-130 Hercules has been one of the most recognisable aircraft in the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), quietly carrying out missions that have shaped Malaysia's defence and humanitarian efforts. The Hercules became the backbone of RMAF's air mobility capability after entering service in 1976. The Hercules fleet has operated with RMAF's No.

items.title: Thousands of US flights snarled before FAA resolves telecom problem
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Thousands of flights across the US were snarled on Monday, with incoming flights halted for hours at major East Coast airports, before the Federal Aviation Administration resolved a telecommunications problem late in the afternoon. The FAA stopped arrivals at all three major New York-area airports as well as Philadelphia and Boston and two smaller airports in the New York area. FlightAware, a flight-tracking website, said about 7,000 flights were delayed or canceled, including 1,400 flights at the three major New York-area airports.

items.title: California declares state of emergency ahead of El Nino
items.summary: LOS ANGELES: California's governor on Monday declared a state of emergency as the US west coast readies for what is expected to be a damaging El Nino. El Nino is the warming phase of a natural cycle in the tropical Pacific, known as the El Nino-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), and comes along every two to seven years. Human-caused climate change can increase El Nino's impacts.

items.title: RMAF scouts C-130J, C-390 to replace ageing Hercules fleet [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lockheed Martin's C-130J and Embraer's C-390 are among the aircraft being discussed as potential replacements for the Royal Malaysian Air Force's (RMAF) ageing C-130 Hercules fleet. He said larger aircraft, including platforms designed for long-range strategic transport missions, might not necessarily suit Malaysia's requirements. he said.

items.title: Stronger prison integrity, security safeguards needed
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The need to strengthen integrity and tighten security procedures in prisons has come under renewed focus amid concerns that weaknesses in the system could facilitate contraband smuggling and undermine inmate rehabilitation. Alliance for a Safe Community chairman Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said integrity among wardens and prison personnel must become part of the prison service's work culture. "Prison officers and wardens are entrusted with a great responsibility of maintaining security, discipline and order within prisons.

items.title: 'Scarce contraband can turn inmates into kings behind bars' [WATCH]
items.summary: Some were known as " peti sejuk " — inmates entrusted with hiding illicit items, he said. LIVING LIKE A KING Thi said inmates controlling illicit items would receive special treatment from fellow prisoners. The task could continue throughout the night, he said.

items.title: 'Tauke', couriers and compromised officers: Inside prison's contraband trade [WATCH]
items.summary: Aziz said most prison officers were professional, but said a small number of compromised people could weaken the system. Orang kerja will deal with the wardens," he said. Orang kerja refers to inmates assigned to work inside the prison.

items.title: Man convicted of attempted murder in shooting of three Palestinian students in Vermont
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A man was convicted by a jury of attempted murder in the late 2023 shooting of three Palestinian American students in Vermont, two of whom were wounded and one was left paralysed from the waist down, prosecutors said on Monday. Jason Eaton was found guilty on three counts of attempted second-degree murder for the shootings of Hisham Awartani, Tahseen Aliahmad and Kinnan Abdalhamid on Nov 25, 2023, in Burlington, Vermont, prosecutor Sarah George, the Chittenden County state's attorney, said in a statement. The conviction rejected Eaton's insanity defence and he will be sentenced at a later time, George said.

items.title: If inflation is falling, why do Malaysians still feel food prices biting hard?
items.summary: Inflation measures how quickly the overall prices of goods and services are rising, rather than whether prices themselves are high or low. When inflation falls, prices can continue to increase — only at a slower pace. The nasi lemak still costs RM5.61, even though inflation has fallen from 10 per cent to 2 per cent.

items.title: ‘This is where we were born’: 9,000 Kampung Bahagia residents wait to rebuild five months after devastating fire
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Sept 22 — Where a thousand wooden stilt houses once rose above the water, only blackened ruins remain. The floating village of Kampung Bahagia here was destroyed by a massive fire on April 19, leaving nearly 9,000 residents with nothing but the clothes on their backs. — Bernama pic Glimmer of hope Rohaida’s family is among the 100 or so families who have been living in the tents since the tragedy, without electricity or a regular supply of clean water.

items.title: Lockheed wins US Army missile contract worth up to US$1.2 billion
items.summary: BENGALURU: Lockheed Martin said on Monday it had secured a contract worth up to US$1.2 billion from the US Army to produce the Increment 2 variant of the Precision Strike Missile (PrSM). PrSM is the Army's next-generation long-range precision strike weapon, designed to replace the Army Tactical Missile System, or ATACMS. The contract comes as Lockheed ramps up production of the Precision Strike Missile amid rising demand for long-range strike weapons.

items.title: Trump praises leftist Mamdani after meeting in New York
items.summary: NEW YORK: President Donald Trump heaped praise Monday onto New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani as the pair set aside their political differences to discuss immigration enforcement and a multi-billion-dollar housing project. I'll be able to say you're going to be a great one, and you're off to a start," Trump told Mamdani at a news conference. "We appreciate the president's commitment to the city," Mamdani said of Trump, who was visiting his hometown New York ahead of the United Nations General Assembly.

items.title: North Korea says it tests new combat weapon system
items.summary: SEOUL: North Korea said it successfully tested a new weapon on Sunday, overseen by leader Kim Jong Un, state media KCNA reported on Tuesday. Kim said the test, carried out by North Korea's Missile Administration, was a demonstration of "ultra-modern" defence technology and showed clear progress in modernising its armed forces, according to KCNA. The South Korean military said on Sunday that North Korea fired two short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast.

items.title: Two pilots die in helicopter crash fighting California wildfire
items.summary: NEW MEXICO: Two pilots died when their helicopter crashed on Sunday afternoon while dropping water on a wildfire in California's Yosemite National Park, authorities said on Monday. Greg King, with contract firm Precision, was one of the pilots who died, according to a statement from the Alaska Division of Forestry and Fire Protection. At least 18 people have died fighting US wildfires so far in 2026, according to data from the Wildland Fire Lessons Learned federal agency.

items.title: Malaysia’s ‘elephant whisperer’ leads push to save Sabah’s endangered Bornean elephants
items.summary: This photo taken on August 24, 2026, shows Farina measuring the length of a female Bornean elephant’s leg during a GPS collaring operation as part of a collaboration involving several agencies near the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. This photo taken on August 25, 2026, shows a wild female Bornean elephant with a GPS collar around her neck crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau. ‘Conflict inevitable’ This photo taken on August 25, 2026, shows a herd of wild Bornean elephants crossing the Kinabatangan River in Sukau.

items.title: Malaysia condemns Houthi attacks, stands in solidarity with Saudi Arabia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Malaysia has condemned in the strongest terms the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, including those targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and expressed solidarity with the Kingdom. Malaysia’s Foreign Ministry said Malaysia supported Saudi Arabia’s efforts to safeguard its sovereignty and territorial integrity, as well as the security and safety of its population, in accordance with the United Nations Charter and international law. The Foreign Ministry said Malaysia reaffirmed the importance of its longstanding partnership with Saudi Arabia and its commitment to further strengthening bilateral ties.

items.title: Five-year-old girl found dead after uncle allegedly throws her into river in Johor
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Sept 21 — A five-year-old girl was found dead, believed to have been thrown into a river by her uncle in Kampung Padang, Tanjung Sedili here, this morning. Kota Tinggi District Police Chief Supt Yusof Othman said police received a report at about 9:30am regarding a 37-year-old local man who went on a rampage armed with a machete while chasing a 40-year-old man. He said initial investigations found that prior to the incident, the suspect was believed to have thrown the victim into the river.

items.title: Anwar leaves Istana Negeri Sembilan after hour-long audience with Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim held a nearly hour-long audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, this evening, as a dispute over the status of the state executive council continued to unfold. Anwar left Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan here after completing the audience, Astro Awani reported. The audience came after Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council members with immediate effect late last night.

items.title: MOH moves on compensation for Sarawak helicopter crash victims’ families, flying doctor service stays grounded
items.summary: TAIPING, Sept 21 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is collaborating with the Public Service Department’s (PSD) Pension Division and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) to ensure a smooth process for granting death ex-gratia payments, retirement benefit claims, and other benefits to the families and heirs of the victims who perished in the flying doctor service (FDS) operation helicopter crash in Sarawak on September 8. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the measure is currently underway to ensure that the surviving next of kin receive appropriate justice and support. The victims who perished were medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, 33, medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, 31, two nurses, Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44, as well as pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30.

items.title: Anwar arrives at Istana Negeri Sembilan for audience with Tuanku Muhriz amid state exco shake-up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — A convoy believed to be carrying Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived at Istana Negeri Sembilan in Changkat Persekutuan here at about 6pm today. Anwar is expected to have an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, following developments over the status of the state executive council (exco). Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim are also expected to have an audience with Tuanku Muhriz.

items.title: Najib’s residence assessed for house arrest, but location not yet finalised, authorities say
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Police and the Prisons Department held a coordination meeting today to assess the security aspects of Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence in preparation for the former prime minister’s house arrest. Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said the meeting between the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the Prisons Department took place at Najib’s residence here, however, clarified that the location for the house arrest has not yet been finalised as the authorities have not yet received the official order document. Sentul district police chief ACP Anuar Bakri Abdul Salam said police are assessing security outside Najib Razak’s residence while the Prisons Department handles detention arrangements.

items.title: Former High Court judge Duncan Sikodol joins MACC Advisory Board
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Former High Court judge Datuk Duncan Sikodol has been appointed to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) Anti-Corruption Advisory Board for the 2026-2029 term. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he presented Duncan with his instrument of appointment today. “May the trust placed in him further strengthen efforts to combat corruption while enhancing the country’s integrity and governance,” Anwar posted on Facebook.

items.title: Cops confirm arson at two 24-hour convenience stores in Kuching
items.summary: Kuching police chief ACP Alexson Naga Chabu said the incidents occurred between 7.05pm and 8.30pm. The fire was extinguished by Fire and Rescue Department (Bomba) personnel. Alexson said police are investigating both incidents under Section 436 of the Penal Code, for mischief by fire or explosive substance with intent to destroy.

items.title: Man found dead in petrol station toilet near Tronoh
items.summary: IPOH, Sept 21 — A 39-year-old local man was found dead inside the toilet of a petrol station in Taman Tronoh Baru, near Tronoh, today. Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) Assistant Director of Operations Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said they received an emergency call at 2:20pm before a team of personnel from the Batu Gajah Fire and Rescue Station (BBP) arrived at the scene at 2:34pm. “Upon arrival, the police and the Ministry of Health (MOH) were already at the scene and found a man lying unconscious, as well as stuck in the toilet door frame.

items.title: ‘Urgent and important’: Serikin border complex fast-tracked for 2027 completion, says minister
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud said the border security project under the National Security Council (MKN) was placed in the ‘urgent and important’ category for fast-track implementation. “This project is also among the matters discussed in the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) Implementation Action Meeting as well as the MA63 Technical Committee Council. “Do not consider projects involving national security as ordinary projects.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh: Loke’s resignation offer was DAP CEC’s final decision, must be respected
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke’s offer to resign as Transport Minister was the final decision of the party’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) and must be respected. DAP CEC deputy secretary-general Hannah Yeoh said the CEC meeting last Saturday also heard various proposals and views before the decision was made. “That was the CEC’s decision.

items.title: Beyond trade: Anwar’s fourth China visit targets AI, digital economy and skills
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 21 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou beginning Tuesday is aimed at deepening economic ties, advancing digital trade frameworks and highlighting the importance of technical talent development. “This is the prime minister’s fourth visit to China (since becoming prime minister in 2022). Anwar, who is also the finance minister, will be accompanied by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Transport Minister Anthony Loke and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

items.title: KL mayor: Sunday flash floods hit city after Ampang, Lembah Keramat record 155mm rainfall
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Flash floods in several parts of the federal capital yesterday were triggered by exceptionally heavy rainfall recorded in the Ampang and Lembah Keramat catchment areas. Kuala Lumpur Mayor Datuk Seri Fadlun Mak Ujud said the 155 millimetres (mm) of rainfall recorded yesterday was more than five times the usual 30 mm in the federal capital. “Observations showed that heavy to very heavy rain was recorded across the Klang Valley yesterday afternoon, particularly in the upstream catchment areas of Ampang, Klang Gates Dam and Lembah Keramat in Selangor.

items.title: Selangor expands Kita Selangor Voucher eligibility, households earning RM8,000 or below now qualify
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 21 — The Selangor government has expanded the eligibility threshold for the Kita Selangor Voucher (BKS) to include households with a monthly income of RM8,000 or below. It initially prioritised vulnerable groups such as single mothers and heads of hardcore-poor households before extending eligibility to households earning RM5,000 or less. “The state government has further expanded the eligibility threshold to include households earning RM8,000 or less.

items.title: JPJ nets RM91.2m from ‘H’ series plates, confirms RM10.7m winning bid for ‘H 1’
items.summary: The next highest was H 9 at RM4,969,999, followed by H 3 at RM4,209,777, H 5 at RM4,007,777 and H 8 at RM4 million. H 6 went for RM3.38 million, H 2 for RM3.18 million and H 7 for RM3.1 million. H 4 fetched RM2,437,777 and H 11 RM1,557,777.

items.title: Putrajaya condemns Al-Aqsa storming, warns provocations risk sparking wider global conflict
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Malaysia strongly condemns the repeated incursions by the Zionist regime into the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound as an extreme provocation that violates the sanctity of al-Haram al-Sharif. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said Al-Aqsa Mosque, as the first qibla and the third holiest site for Muslims, must be defended. The statement came after about 100 Israeli settlers reportedly entered the Al-Aqsa Mosque compound on Sunday under tight security by Israeli security forces, ahead of the Yom Kippur observance.

items.title: 1MDB seeks Federal Court ruling, says Malaysia should hear fraud claims against UK law firm
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) has filed an application seeking leave to appeal the appellate court’s ruling that the High Court lacked the jurisdiction to hear its lawsuit against a UK law firm. She also told Bernama that the Federal Court has fixed October 12 to hear the leave to appeal application. 1MDB has put forward 24 questions of law concerning jurisdiction and consolidation of its suit in seeking leave to appeal from the Federal Court.

items.title: ‘Possibly the most effective transport minister’: Lim Guan Eng praises Loke’s RM21b infrastructure legacy in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 21 — DAP Air Putih assemblyman Lim Guan Eng said today that Transport Minister Anthony Loke’s impending departure from the federal Cabinet represents a major loss for Penang, crediting him with securing federal approval for more than RM21 billion in critical transport infrastructure for the state. In a press statement, the former Penang chief minister detailed the federal investments championed by Loke during his ministerial tenure. “With RM 21 billion of approved transportation projects in Penang, Loke is possibly the most effective transport minister who has done the most for Penang compared to the series of MCA transport ministers before him,” Lim said.

items.title: Former deputy minister Datuk Yahya Lampong dies at 86
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 21 — Former deputy rural development minister Datuk Yahya Lampong, who also served as the Kota Belud Member of Parliament, died at the age of 86 at KPJ Ampang Puteri Specialist Hospital, Kuala Lumpur, at about 6am today. The death was confirmed by his son, Masley Yahya, in a Facebook post today, although the cause of death has yet to be confirmed. Yahya served as the Kota Belud MP from 1982 to 1986 after winning the seat as an independent candidate in the 1982 General Election.

items.title: Malaysia’s air quality improves slightly, but Kapit and Serian remain shrouded in haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 21 — Air quality in Kapit, Sarawak, deteriorated steadily throughout the day, overtaking other hotspots to become the most polluted location in Malaysia as of 4pm today. Nationwide, a total of 17 monitoring stations remained in the “Unhealthy” bracket (API 101 to 200), down from the 21 affected stations reported earlier in the morning. Sarawak accounts for majority of affected areas Sarawak remained by far the hardest-hit state, accounting for 10 of the 17 unhealthy stations nationwide.

items.title: Deepavali Bazaar fees slashed 85pc, Hannah Yeoh sets RM400 cap in Brickfields
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 21 — Participation fees for Kuala Lumpur’s 2026 Deepavali Bazaar have been cut by 85 per cent to a maximum of RM400, including the deposit, as part of efforts to reduce costs for traders. This year’s RM400 fee comprises a RM30 licence fee, RM150 service charge, RM150 site rental and RM70 deposit. In comparison, traders had to pay RM2,626 in 2025, comprising a RM21 licence fee, RM105 service charge, RM500 site rental and RM2,000 deposit.
